transcript.text: I've just bought an AEG L7FEE865R and the Eco 40-60 wash says 3:39 and seems to take forever. My old machine did a 40 wash in an hour. Is it faulty? Should I send it back?

It is very unlikely to be faulty; Eco 40-60 cycles are designed to run for three or four hours to save energy, so your machine is behaving normally compared to older models. The display time also adjusts dynamically as it weighs the laundry and balances the load during the wash. To rule out any genuine heating issues, please switch off and unplug the machine before checking that the door is firmly shut and nothing is caught in the seal. Then run a standard 60°C cottons programme with a normal load and check if the clothes come out warm when it finishes.
Ok, I can run a 60 cottons if needed. For what it's worth the Cottons 40 programme only shows about 2 hours, and the clothes do come out clean from the Eco one. Does that change anything?

That suggests it is working normally, as Eco programmes are specifically designed to run longer at lower temperatures to save energy and water. The 2-hour Cottons 40 cycle is much shorter because it uses higher heat and more intense washing action. Since your clothes come out clean and the machine completes the cycle without error codes, there is no need to send it back. You can simply use the standard cotton programmes for faster washes if you prefer speed over energy efficiency.
